title: Best Meeting Point
summary: For an m x n grid with each 1 indicating a friend's home, find the meeting point that minimizes the total Manhattan distance to all homes.
statement: For an m x n grid with each 1 indicating a friend's home, find the meeting point that minimizes the total Manhattan distance to all homes. The total distance is the sum of the Manhattan distances from each home to the meeting point.
constraints: grid is a rectangular 1–200 by 1–200 matrix containing only 0 and 1, with at least one home marked 1.
Return the minimum sum of four-direction Manhattan distances from every home to one meeting cell. The meeting cell may be any grid cell.
hints: Manhattan distance separates into an independent row distance plus an independent column distance.
For one-dimensional absolute distances, every median minimizes the total; the mean is not generally optimal.
Collect all home rows in row-major order and collect/sort all home columns. Sum distances to the median of each list.
Row-major scanning already sorts row coordinates. Sorting only the columns gives O(h log h), where h is the number of homes.
editorial: For any meeting cell (r,c), the total is the sum of |home_row-r| plus the separate sum of |home_column-c|. A median minimizes each one-dimensional absolute-distance sum, so choosing the row median and column median is globally optimal. Row-major traversal yields sorted rows; columns are sorted explicitly. The independent oracle evaluates every possible meeting cell on small generated grids.

tests.explanation: Choosing row 0 and column 2 gives distances 2, 2, and 2, for the minimum total 6.
Any cell between the two endpoint homes has total distance 5, so the minimum is 5.
